statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. With CME equity index futures shut since Friday 21:00 UTC there is no live Nasdaq-100 price path to score, so Tail remains far below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on an escalating US-Iran naval exchange around the Strait of Hormuz and a hawkish front-end rates backdrop.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the whole outlook; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: No live Nasdaq-100 price path six hours before the 22:00 UTC reopen, with the US-Iran naval exchange now extending to a targeted carrier and an explicit Iranian warning of heavier responses
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range against a 29,482.30 previous close, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53 after a contained 13.80-14.58 day range. Friday's internals were rotational rather than directional, with semiconductors broadly higher while several megacaps fell, which argues against an aligned one-way regime being carried into the reopen. The geopolitical picture verified this hour is a step more serious than a tanker exchange alone: CENTCOM permanently disabled two Iranian oil tankers and destroyed a third after Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps fired several ballistic missiles toward a US aircraft carrier and an accompanying destroyer, neither of which was hit. Iran's IRGC navy then said it had struck three tankers on unauthorised Strait routes plus three US-linked vessels, and on Sunday claimed an attack on an unmanned US vessel that Washington has not confirmed. Iran's parliament speaker stated that the era of proportionate responses is over and that further responses would be faster, heavier and more painful. Independent tracking still contradicts official claims of normalised transit, with Kpler counts of roughly six vessels midweek against far higher pre-war norms. The energy channel remains the sharper Stress input: Brent settled Friday at $96.28, its highest since July 24 and more than 8% higher on the week, and US diesel set an all-time high near $5.85 a gallon with distillate stockpiles at record lows entering the heating season. The rates backdrop is the second Stress channel, with H.15 for September 3 showing the 2-year at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77% and market odds on a September hike described as close to even. Under the tail definition none of this is observed price-path evidence: while the venue is shut there is no measurable pullback depth, failed retracement, repeated extension or extreme-hold, so Tail is held at 5 in the low band and Stress at 57 in the elevated band. Conditional risk concentrates in the single 22:00 UTC reopen hour, where the accumulated weekend headline stack would reprice into the thinnest depth of the week; that hour is scored at Tail 22 and maps to WATCH before decaying as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. US cash equities and the Treasury market are closed on September 7 for Labor Day and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout, so no scheduled US catalyst falls inside the outlook window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held in a narrow 4-5 band with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress oscillated between 52 and 57 across the weekend closure, easing during the Asian overnight and firming again through the European and US Sunday hours to finish the window at 56. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour, reflecting a closed venue rather than an observed regime.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover six further closed hours, the scheduled 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday with no US cash open inside the window. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the two hours around the reopen, which reach 22 and 20 and map to WATCH where the unresolved Hormuz escalation and the hawkish front end would meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 65 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 52. No US macro release falls inside the window, US cash equities and the Treasury market are closed on September 7 for Labor Day and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI and Oracle earnings on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
